I am 79 this year. I have farmed my whole life on these flat fields in Quzhou County, and I know what my body and my land can still handle. My children work in the city now, so it is just me and my wife at home. We have a little over 4 mu of land, and I am not going to try anything new or risky at my age.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, like I have done for decades. I cannot manage cotton anymore—it needs too much spraying and picking, and my back cannot take it. The wheat went into the ground last October after I ran the rotary tiller. I bought improved wheat seeds from the supply shop in town. For fertilizer, I spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, and I will topdress with urea when the wheat starts jointing in the spring. I will irrigate four times: now as the wheat greens up, once at jointing, once at flowering, and once during grain filling. If the aphids show up, I will spray insecticide—probably twice this season.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant denghai605 maize directly into the wheat stubble without plowing. Everyone uses no-tillage now; it saves time and diesel. I will put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing. If the summer rains are good, I may only need to irrigate twice, but I will watch the sky. I will spray for weeds and insects once or twice if I see problems.

I expect to harvest about 1,000 jin per mu of wheat and about the same for maize. That is what I have gotten most years, and at 79 I do not gamble on new varieties or strange methods. I stick to what this soil and these hands have always given me.
